buttonLabel: "Adventures in Argentina, Ecuador and Peru: explore the itinerary"
lead: >-
  In Argentina, travellers follow the walkways at Iguazu Falls;
  in Peru, they visit high-altitude Lake Titicaca and Machu Picchu;
  and in Ecuador, they head to the Galapagos Islands. These are three
  very different kinds of adventure: guided walks, journeys through
  the Andes and a boat trip to the islands. The itinerary does not
  include a sporting trek to Machu Picchu or scuba diving in the Galapagos.
---

## What brings Argentina, Ecuador and Peru together

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} connecting these countries with the theme of adventure. One option is the [extended journey across eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Argentina, Peru and Ecuador do not come one immediately after another: Argentina is followed by Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia, then Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. This is **a selection of countries within a long itinerary**, not a separate three-country trip.

Three contrasts stand out. At Iguazu, you are surrounded by humid subtropical forest and immense waterfalls. In Peru, the altitude of the Andes, visits to Titicaca and the cultural heritage of Machu Picchu shape the experience. In the Galapagos, you discover nature from a boat, during landings and on short island walks. However, **the itinerary does not specify a multi-day camping trek, specialist mountaineering training or certified scuba diving in these three countries**.

The clearest off-road section of the entire journey is actually in Bolivia: after San Pedro de Atacama, there is a two-day 4×4 jeep journey across high-altitude lagoons and salt flats. It belongs to the full eight-country tour, even though Bolivia is not part of the selected Argentina + Ecuador + Peru combination. For itineraries without a thematic filter, see the [general three-country selection](/multi-country/argentina_ecuador_peru/). Other forms of active travel appear in the [multi-country adventure catalogue](/multi-country/interests/adventure/).

## Argentina: walking the trails of Iguazu National Park

On the Argentine side of Iguazu, a group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide departs from the [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) area. Visitor walkways and viewing platforms offer views of the cascades amid their natural surroundings. It is an exhilarating part of the journey, but its format differs from a sporting river descent: **rafting and canyoning are not included in the Argentine day**.

The Brazilian side of Iguazu is visited the previous day. There, the Bird Park and Macuco Safari are listed as optional paid activities, not as part of the mandatory Argentine excursion. After the Argentine falls, the itinerary continues by air to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), with city sightseeing and tango on the programme.

The time needed for the walkways depends on park operations, water levels and the condition of individual viewing areas. In 2026, Argentina's national parks authority restricted access to some sections when the water rose. Access to the Devil's Throat viewpoint should therefore be checked for your travel dates. For longer nature-based activities, compare the [adventure programmes in Argentina](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/) with your preferred activity.

## Peru: Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu at altitude

The Peru section begins with an overland border crossing from Bolivia to [Lake Titicaca and Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). A visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) is included. The group then travels by tourist coach to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), stopping for sightseeing and lunch along the way. The next day is devoted to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), visited on a group excursion with an English-speaking guide, with the return by train.

The adventure here comes from changing elevations, mountain scenery and historical sites. **Travelling to Machu Picchu by train is not the same as hiking the Inca Trail**. The published itinerary does not include a four-day trek, overnight camping, an independent mountaineering route or the separate arrangements those activities require.

A significant consideration is the accumulated exposure to altitude. Even before Peru, the route crosses Bolivia's highlands, in places above 4,000 metres. Titicaca and Cusco follow. Travellers who struggle with altitude or have significant medical restrictions should discuss this part with a doctor beforehand and clarify the arrangements for rest and transfers. Being comfortable with ordinary city excursions is no guarantee of feeling well in the mountains.

Entry to Machu Picchu is managed through tickets and designated visitor circuits; the official booking system allows visitors to select specific admission options. It is important to check your ticket, the circuit within the complex and the actual excursion time. Travellers looking specifically for a high-altitude hike should separately compare [adventure tours in Peru](/interests/adventure/tours/peru/) that include walking routes.

## Ecuador: from high-altitude Quito to ocean islands

The Ecuador section begins with a flight from Lima to [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), where a sightseeing day includes the historic centre and the equator line. Quito is a high-altitude city; walking and long transfers may feel different from those at sea level. However, **climbing Cotopaxi volcano is not part of this tour**: the fact that a volcano appears in the name of one geographical page on the site does not make a summit ascent part of the itinerary.

Next comes a flight to the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). On [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), the programme includes its highlands and a transfer to Puerto Ayora. The following day features a boat excursion with **one of two possible routes**: [North Seymour Island](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach, or [South Plaza Island](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Punta Carrion. Both alternatives are not promised together; the actual choice is confirmed when booking.

Here, adventure centres on the sea, nature trails and wildlife watching. On North Seymour, you may see seabirds including frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies; the Ecuadorian archipelago is also home to iguanas, tortoises and sea lions. But the presence of a species in a protected area **does not guarantee a sighting at a particular time**. Landings and routes depend on permits and sea conditions.

If the confirmed option offers snorkelling, this is a separate marine activity with its own conditions. **Snorkelling is not scuba diving**, and certified dives cannot be promised on the basis of an island excursion. National park rules require travellers to follow guide instructions, maintain a safe distance from wildlife and observe restrictions in protected areas. For further active journeys, browse the [Ecuador adventure catalogue](/interests/adventure/tours/ecuador/).

## Three different kinds of exertion: what to compare before booking

| Where | Actual format |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Guided walkways at Iguazu |
| Peru | High-altitude road journeys, Titicaca, Machu Picchu |
| Ecuador | Flight to the Galapagos and boat excursion |

Someone who finds a walk near waterfalls easy may react very differently to Titicaca's altitude. Equally, someone who enjoys mountain terrain may feel uncomfortable on a sea crossing. On a long trip, it is useful to discuss both considerations and opportunities to rest between busy days. The main off-road jeep section takes place in Bolivia, so **all eight countries** need to be considered.

Your luggage needs to cover humid Iguazu, cool highlands and sunny boat excursions. Non-slip shoes, rain and sun protection, and a light warm layer for altitude are sensible choices. Specific water-related equipment depends on the island itinerary selected and confirmed. There is no reason to buy a mountaineering kit or scuba gear for activities not included in the programme.

There are many transport stages: domestic flights, an overland border crossing, a tourist coach, a train and boat transfers. Planning requires time allowances and checks of entry, transit and conservation rules based on each traveller's citizenship and dates. We can coordinate specific itinerary details and help you assess whether the level of exertion suits your preferred travel style. The complete route and the current tour's terms are below:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Argentina, Ecuador and Peru

### Is the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu included?

No. The confirmed programme includes a group visit to Machu Picchu and a return to Cusco by train. A multi-day hiking trek is not included.

### Can I climb Cotopaxi in Ecuador?

The tour includes sightseeing in Quito followed by the Galapagos Islands. Climbing the volcano is not one of the described activities and must not be treated as included.

### Is there scuba diving in the Galapagos?

A boat excursion follows one of two routes. Certified scuba diving is not included; possible snorkelling depends on the specific option confirmed.

### Where is the most demanding off-road section?

Between Chile and Bolivia, with a two-day 4×4 jeep journey past high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni. This section belongs to the complete tour, although Bolivia is not one of the three countries in the filter.

### Is the itinerary suitable without mountaineering experience?

No technical ascent is included in Argentina, Ecuador or Peru. However, the altitudes of Bolivia and Peru, numerous flights, boat crossings and busy schedule call for appropriate fitness and preparation.

## Argentina, Peru and Ecuador: three cultural stories on one long journey

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining Argentina, Peru and Ecuador with a cultural and historical focus. The [32-day tour of eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) links these destinations with Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Colombia. After Argentina, travellers visit several other countries before reaching Peru; they then fly from Lima to Ecuador. Thus, the selected trio represents **part of an eight-country journey**, not a short route between just three capitals.

The differences become particularly clear in the excursions. [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) is experienced through its neighbourhoods and tango. [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) tell the story of the Inca Empire. Quito offers colonial architecture and a blend of local and European artistic traditions. For a comparison without the cultural filter, see the [Argentina–Ecuador–Peru selection](/multi-country/argentina_ecuador_peru/); for other thematic journeys, browse [multi-country cultural itineraries](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/).

| Country | Cultural experiences during the journey |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Buenos Aires neighbourhoods and tango |
| Peru | Titicaca, the Incas and colonial Lima |
| Ecuador | Historic Quito and the equator line |

## Argentina: Buenos Aires and the living tradition of tango

The first day in Argentina is devoted to Iguazu Falls, followed by a flight to the capital. In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the programme includes a three-hour group sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide. The route covers [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/), [San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/), Plaza de Mayo, Casa Rosada, Recoleta and Puerto Madero.

These districts reveal how the city developed: port neighbourhoods, old squares and markets, grand architecture and a modern waterfront. One sightseeing day provides an overview but does not replace independent visits to several museums. In the evening, the programme features a [tango show with dinner](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-with-dinner/), a chance to experience Argentina's music and stage culture. A tango lesson is not included that day.

The Argentine side of Iguazu is part of the same journey as a nature excursion. The waterfalls add variety, but the country's cultural experiences are centred chiefly on Buenos Aires. More options appear among [cultural and historical tours including Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/).

## Peru: from reed islands to Inca monuments

The Peru section begins after an overland crossing from Bolivia at Desaguadero. Near [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), travellers visit the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) with an English-speaking guide. This offers an introduction to local ways of life and customs, a cultural experience very different from the urban excursion in Argentina.

A special tourist coach then takes the group to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), with stops at Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, La Raya and Pucara. The journey occupies a full day and introduces the historical geography of the Andes. Next comes a [Machu Picchu excursion](/peru/cusco/machu-picchu-day-tour-from-cusco/) with an English-speaking guide and a train journey back. Lunch is included on this excursion day. **A multi-day hike along the Inca Trail is not included.**

In Cusco, the group also visits Coricancha, Qenqo, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay and Sacsayhuaman. After a flight to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), the route takes in Miraflores, the historic centre, Plaza Mayor and Santo Domingo. The Cathedral can be replaced by a visit to the MALI museum if it is closed. These days make it possible to compare pre-colonial heritage with architecture from later periods. For a journey focused above all on the Incas, compare [cultural tours of Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/).

## Ecuador: Quito's colonial architecture and nature on the islands

The group flies from Lima to Quito. Ecuador's capital is known for its churches, monasteries and artistic traditions dating from the colonial period. UNESCO has inscribed the city on the World Heritage List. The published itinerary includes a [tour of Quito and the equator line](/ecuador/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/quito-panecillo-and-equator/), covering the historic centre, [Mitad del Mundo](/ecuador/place/mitad-del-mundo/) and the [Intiñan Museum](/ecuador/place/intinan-museum/).

Then another chapter begins: the Galapagos Islands, Santa Cruz Island, Puerto Ayora and a boat excursion. The island day offers **one of two alternatives**: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Punta Carrion. This is a nature programme, not a historical or architectural one, and the choice is confirmed at booking. If culture and museums are your priority, it is worth discussing how much time to spend on the islands and which itinerary is most suitable.

## Planning time and transfers between cultural stops

Cultural days alternate with major transport stages. Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia lie between Argentina and Peru, including high-altitude regions; a flight connects Peru's Lima with Ecuador's Quito. There are high mountain passes on the Puno–Cusco route, while Quito sits at about 2,800 metres. The pace calls for preparation, particularly if you want to visit museums beyond the included excursions.

Entry and transit rules must be checked separately for each traveller's citizenship across every country on the full itinerary. Baggage and connections likewise need to be planned for the complete eight-country programme, not just the three countries shown in the filter. We help coordinate the sequence of stops, time for acclimatisation and sensible margins between flights.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Frequently asked questions about cultural tours through Argentina, Peru and Ecuador

### Can I visit only these three countries?

This selection features an [eight-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) including five additional nations. A separate journey limited to Argentina, Peru and Ecuador would require a bespoke itinerary to be agreed.

### Is tango included in the Argentina excursions?

Yes. In Buenos Aires, there is a [tango show with dinner](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-with-dinner/). This is attendance at a performance, not a dance class.

### How does the Machu Picchu visit work?

The programme includes a day excursion from [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) with an English-speaking guide, lunch and a return by train. A multi-day walking trek is not included.

### Are both Galapagos island-excursion options included?

Only one alternative programme is scheduled for that day. The specific option is confirmed at booking, so both trips cannot be promised together.

## Argentina, Ecuador and Peru: from Iguazu to the Galapagos

**In this combination, the nature experiences are spread across places that lie very far apart.** [Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) in Argentina means waterfalls surrounded by subtropical forest; [Puno and Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) in Peru mean a high-altitude lake; and the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) in Ecuador are a volcanic archipelago with specific rules for watching wildlife.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. This is a [32-day journey across eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also visiting Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Colombia. Ada Tours does not offer a separate direct three-country route between Argentina, Peru and Ecuador within this selection. The actual sequence matters: after Argentina, travellers cross other countries on their way to the Peruvian Andes, then fly to Ecuador.

For a broader choice of destinations, see [nature tours of Argentina](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/), [Peru](/interests/nature/tours/peru/) and [Ecuador](/interests/nature/tours/ecuador/). Here we focus on how these places fit together in one particular extended programme.

## Argentina: Iguazu cascades and a limited nature section

On day 7 of the Argentina section, the programme visits [Iguazu Falls from Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Walkways lead through humid vegetation to different viewpoints overlooking the cascades. The day before, travellers see the Brazilian side from [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The two visits concern the same waterfall system but offer different perspectives.

The itinerary then moves to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), where sightseeing days focus on urban history and cultural neighbourhoods. **Patagonian glaciers or trekking in El Chalten should not be added to this 32-day programme**: Argentina is included, but the confirmed nature section in the country is concentrated at Iguazu.

This is an important distinction when choosing a tour. If [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) is essential to your plans, you will need a different itinerary with an actual stop at El Calafate.

## Peru: Titicaca, the Andes and Machu Picchu

Peru comes closer to the middle of the journey, after Bolivia's high-altitude section. On day 16, travellers journey from La Paz via Tiwanaku to Puno and visit the Uros Islands on [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The following day is devoted to the journey to Cusco, with stops along the way.

Day 18 includes an excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The archaeological complex has a striking natural setting of mountain slopes, deep valleys and the humid vegetation of the eastern Andes. However, this is an organised visit to an archaeological site, and **the multi-day Inca Trail is not automatically included**. Any hiking element depends on the confirmed visitor circuit and valid admission ticket.

Changes in altitude must not be overlooked. Bolivia, Puno and Cusco call for acclimatisation. Travellers may spend much of a day in a coach, but that does not remove the effects of thinner air. Anyone with a history of difficulty at altitude should discuss individual preparations with a doctor.

## Ecuador: Santa Cruz and a Galapagos excursion

After Lima, the itinerary reaches [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). Ecuador's nature section begins on day 23 with a flight to the archipelago and accommodation on [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), including its [highland areas](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/). This is a completely different environment from the Peruvian Andes.

Day 24 features **one of two alternative programmes**, not a visit to every island. The first combines [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) with [Bachas Beaches](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/); the second combines [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) with [Punta Carrion](/ecuador/place/punta-carrion/). The actual option must be confirmed when arranging the trip. It would be incorrect to promise all four places in a single day.

In the Galapagos, it is especially important to follow the official rules of the protected area: stay on authorised routes, follow licensed guides' instructions, keep your distance from wildlife and do not feed animals. A species or its behaviour cannot be guaranteed merely because an island is associated with it. [Ecuador nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/ecuador/) provide other itineraries to compare with this format.

## Comparing nature experiences by day

| Section | Nature highlight |
|---|---|
| Argentina, day 7 | Iguazu, walkways and cascades |
| Peru, days 16–18 | Titicaca and Machu Picchu |
| Ecuador, days 23–25 | Santa Cruz and the selected island excursion |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The table compares different types of visits, not the amount of time spent inside each natural park. For example, there is a flight between Peru and Ecuador, and after the Galapagos the journey continues to Colombia. Confirming the individual excursions and their durations matters more than a single overall figure of “32 days”.

## What to consider when preparing

For Iguazu, bring comfortable shoes and rain protection. In the Andes, warm clothing, sun protection and attention to how you feel at altitude matter. In the Galapagos, visitors must consider biosecurity rules, baggage restrictions, access to visitor sites and permitted activities on the islands. The itinerary includes overland borders, domestic flights and a boat excursion, so you should not assume that one baggage policy applies throughout.

**Restrictions on individual Galapagos visitor sites and the specific alternative island route need to be confirmed before travelling.** Similarly, re-entry requirements must be checked for the traveller's citizenship across every country on the itinerary, not just the three destinations named in the catalogue.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a trip covering only Argentina, Ecuador and Peru in this selection?

At present, the selection includes a 32-day journey across eight countries. The three countries in the filter are part of its main geography.

### Does the itinerary include both North Seymour and South Plaza?

No. The Galapagos day offers an alternative: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Punta Carrion. The final choice must be confirmed.

### Can I expect to visit Perito Moreno in Argentina?

Not on this itinerary. The nature stop in Argentina is Iguazu; Patagonia's glaciers belong to other confirmed itineraries.

## What nature experiences do Argentina, Ecuador and Peru offer?

Our themed selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [“Eight South American countries in 32 days” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) connects Argentina, Ecuador and Peru with Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Colombia. Among the selected trio, the “Wildlife and Safari” theme is most clearly represented by the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The [Argentine side of Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and [Puno and Lake Titicaca region](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) primarily offer scenery and landscapes, which also fall under the separate “Nature” theme.

Each section has a different focus. At Iguazu, the main attraction is the waterfalls and humid subtropical forest. In the Galapagos, attention shifts to island animals and marine life. Titicaca is a high-altitude lake where the programme also introduces the culture of local communities. A wildlife theme does not make every stop a safari or a specialist birdwatching tour.

The countries must not be confused: between Argentina and Peru, the journey crosses Chile and Bolivia; Ecuador follows Peru. This is the established sequence of one extended trip, not direct flights between three chosen nature areas.

## Argentina: Iguazu and the Upper Parana Atlantic Forest

The itinerary includes both sides of Iguazu Falls. Argentina's national park is in Misiones Province and protects parts of the humid Upper Parana Atlantic Forest. Visitor trails and viewing platforms reveal the falls from different angles, while the surrounding vegetation is part of a wider ecosystem inhabited by birds and mammals.

Travellers come here primarily for the waterfalls. A toucan, coati or another animal may appear near the trail, but sightings cannot be guaranteed. Photograph wildlife from a distance, do not feed animals and follow park restrictions. Some paths are close to the water, where the conditions are humid and surfaces may be slippery.

For a rewarding nature excursion, time on the park trails and the availability of viewpoints matter more than a general promise to see every animal of the region. Current restrictions, opening hours and weather should be checked for the date of your visit.

## Peru: Titicaca and the transition to a different Andean environment

The Peru section of the extended journey goes through [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), then Cusco, [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lima. At Titicaca, travellers discover the floating Uros Islands and the high-altitude lakeside environment. This combines scenery with a cultural excursion.

The lake is at considerable altitude, so even gentle outings by the water call for acclimatisation to thinner air. An ordinary trip to the Uros Islands does not amount to a separate multi-day birdwatching itinerary or guaranteed sightings of specific bird species.

This 32-day programme does not include a dedicated cruise in the Peruvian Amazon. Such journeys are available separately, but they cannot be added to the description of this tour simply because it carries the “Wildlife and Safari” theme. If Peru's tropical forests are your principal goal, compare [nature tours including Peru](/interests/nature/tours/peru/) rather than expecting an Amazon section on every journey through Lima and Cusco.

## Ecuador: Santa Cruz and the marine wildlife of the Galapagos

In Ecuador, the itinerary visits Quito first, then continues to the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). After arriving, travellers transfer to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and explore the island and its highlands.

For the next day there are **two alternative excursions**, one of which is selected for the particular journey:

- [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach: an introduction to island birdlife, the coast and marine environments.
- South Plaza and Punta Carrion: a different island route combining wildlife observation on land with a marine section.

The alternatives cannot be combined into one mandatory excursion or sold as visits to all four places in a day. The chosen option depends on the confirmed programme, vessel operations and current permits. After the Galapagos section, travellers return to the mainland via Guayaquil and continue their journey through Colombia.

The Galapagos are particularly rewarding for watching animals that are often less wary of people than their mainland counterparts. Yet an animal's proximity does not give visitors permission to touch it. National park authorities require visitors to **keep at least 2 metres away**, follow authorised routes, avoid feeding wildlife and use approved guides and operators.

## Comparing the nature sections

| Part of the route | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Argentine Iguazu | Waterfalls and humid forest |
| Peruvian Titicaca | High-altitude lake |
| Galapagos, Ecuador | Island and marine wildlife |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

For someone travelling to see wildlife, **the amount of actual time spent in each ecosystem** is important. At Iguazu, the programme concentrates on the established visitor routes around the falls. At Titicaca, it features a lake and cultural excursion. In the Galapagos, it visits protected island habitats, but the number of days is limited by the overall 32-day schedule.

For waterfalls and mountain lakes, compare [nature tours including Argentina](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/) and [Peru](/interests/nature/tours/peru/). For island wildlife, look at [Ecuador “Wildlife and Safari” tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/). All combinations of these three countries with other themes are gathered in the [Argentina + Ecuador + Peru catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_ecuador_peru/).

## Flights, entry requirements and conservation documents

The extended itinerary includes international flights and several changes of climate. Moving from humid Iguazu Falls to high-altitude Peru and island Ecuador calls for different clothing and careful baggage planning. Light clothing and splash protection are useful at Iguazu, warm layers and acclimatisation in the Andes, and sun protection and suitable footwear for coastal walks in the Galapagos.

Visiting the Galapagos involves formalities beyond the general entry requirements for Ecuador. The archipelago's Governing Council requires a **Tarjeta de Control de Tránsito (TCT)**, and a conservation entrance fee is charged for access to protected areas. Current amounts, procedures and whether these charges are included in a particular tour price should be checked before travelling. Airport biosecurity measures also restrict the import of certain foods and natural materials.

Requirements for Russian citizens and travellers with other passports must be checked individually for Argentina, Peru, Ecuador and every country in between. Citizenship, transit routing and document validity all matter. Travellers should also establish which payment cards will work and how to cover personal expenses in each country: Argentine pesos, Peruvian soles and US dollars in Ecuador are not a single payment system.

Ada Tours helps coordinate the order of flights, border crossings and nature excursions. Wildlife encounters, weather conditions and border officers' decisions cannot be guaranteed in advance.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Ecuador and Peru

### Can I see both Iguazu and the Galapagos on this journey?

Yes. Both are included in the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), along with Titicaca and stops in other countries.

### Are both Galapagos excursion options included?

No. The itinerary provides a choice: North Seymour and Bachas **or** South Plaza and Punta Carrion. The specific option is agreed for the selected departure.

### Is there an Amazon cruise in Peru?

Not on this 32-day itinerary. The Peru section includes Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima.

### Can I approach Galapagos animals for a photograph?

No. Official rules require a distance of at least 2 metres and prohibit disturbing wildlife even when the animals come close on their own.

### Do I need additional documents for the Galapagos?

Yes. Visits to the archipelago require a TCT and involve a separate conservation fee. Current application arrangements and payment terms should be checked before travelling.

## Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Ecuador: how the itinerary actually unfolds

The combination of [Argentina](/argentina/), [Uruguay](/uruguay/), [Peru](/peru/) and [Ecuador](/ecuador/) is best considered through three distinct experiences. Around the Río de la Plata, you visit cities in two neighbouring countries; in the Andes, you explore Inca heritage; and in Ecuador, you continue to the volcanic Galapagos Islands. These places cannot, however, be joined by a short road trip.

Our catalogue contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring all four as **principal** countries. The main programme is [“Eight South American countries in 32 days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Alongside these four, it includes Brazil, Chile, Bolivia and Colombia. The journey starts in São Paulo and Rio, then visits Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Montevideo, Chile and Bolivia, continues through Peru and Ecuador, and finishes in Colombia. Choosing this selection means choosing a combination of countries, not a separate self-contained four-country tour.

## Argentina and Uruguay: a return ferry trip to Montevideo in one day

After visiting the Brazilian side of Iguazu, the route goes via [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) to the Argentine falls and then onward to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). Here, a sightseeing tour of the city's districts and an evening tango show with dinner are planned.

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited from Buenos Aires by ferry: an early transfer to the port, a crossing of the Río de la Plata estuary, sightseeing with an English-speaking guide, free time and the return ferry on the same day. Ferry tickets are included in the described programme. This is **a one-day visit to Uruguay**, not several nights on the Uruguayan coast.

For that day, you must allow for your passport and border checks in both directions, ferry check-in times and travel from the hotel to the port. Dinner or extra stops in Montevideo should not be promised beyond the published itinerary. Travellers who also want to see Colonia del Sacramento or Punta del Este will need to agree on a longer Uruguay section.

## Peru: from Lake Titicaca to Machu Picchu

On the full itinerary, Peru begins after La Paz in Bolivia: an overland journey via Tiwanaku and the Desaguadero border crossing leads to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). A tourist coach then takes the group to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), with stops en route.

A full-day visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is planned from Cusco with an English-speaking guide; the train ticket and lunch are included in the specific tour's terms. After visiting Cusco's archaeological monuments, the route continues to Lima and then by air to Quito.

The principal practical change in Peru is the altitude. Overnight stays around Titicaca and Cusco are at high elevations, so travellers should discuss how they tolerate altitude, the rate of ascent and suitable exertion before departure. Their past response to altitude matters more than general sporting fitness. Symptoms of altitude sickness require medical assessment before continuing an ascent.

## Ecuador: Quito, Santa Cruz and a choice of island excursion

The Ecuador section begins in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) with a visit to the equator area. The group then flies to the Galapagos, arriving via Baltra and staying on [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The itinerary includes the island's highlands and **one of two alternative** marine routes: North Seymour with Bachas Beach or South Plaza with Punta Carrion. This is a choice of confirmed itinerary, not a promise to visit all four places.

Separate rules apply to the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/): visitors obtain a Transit Control Card (TCT), undergo biosecurity baggage inspection and pay the applicable conservation entrance fee on arrival. These procedures are additional to Ecuador's general immigration requirements. Allow time for them before the island flight from Quito or Guayaquil.

After the islands, the route returns to [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/) and continues to Colombia. Ecuador's US dollar makes cash calculations simpler than using Argentine pesos, Uruguayan pesos and Peruvian soles, although whether a foreign bank card works depends on the bank, payment network and individual merchant.

## Documents, budget and luggage for these four countries

Travellers holding Russian international passports should check the entry requirements for Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Ecuador **for their specific departure date** before buying tickets: permitted duration of stay, passport requirements, proof of onward or return travel and the rules for re-entering Argentina on the day of the ferry trip. For other nationalities, those requirements need to be checked separately. The Galapagos travel rules form another set of requirements.

| Stage | Special consideration |
|---|---|
| Buenos Aires – Montevideo | Ferry, passport control and return time |
| Puno – Cusco – Lima | Altitude, intercity travel and the train to Machu Picchu |
| Quito – Galapagos | TCT, biosecurity, island flights and fees |

Day-to-day expenses involve four currency situations: Argentine and Uruguayan pesos, the Peruvian sol and US dollars in Ecuador. Check ways to pay at each stage and carry appropriate cash for small expenses; not every Russian or foreign card can be assumed to work everywhere. Your main suitcase needs to suit warm Buenos Aires, cool Andean evenings and sunny island walks. Restrictions on carrying food and natural materials are particularly important for the islands.

We help align schedules, excursions and documents with your chosen dates, keeping the distinction between confirmed tour inclusions and possible individual modifications clear.

## Frequently asked questions about Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Ecuador

### Can I visit only these four countries and skip the others?

A separate itinerary would need to be designed for that journey. The published programme featuring these four also travels through Brazil, Chile, Bolivia and Colombia, so its overall duration cannot be treated as time spent in only the four selected countries.

### How long do we spend in Uruguay?

The described tour includes one day travelling by ferry from Buenos Aires to Montevideo and back. An overnight stay in Uruguay is not scheduled.

### Do we visit both North Seymour and South Plaza in the Galapagos?

No. The tour includes one of two alternative excursions. The selected island route is confirmed at booking.

### What is the most demanding transfer between Peru and Ecuador?

On the published itinerary it is the Lima–Quito flight after a busy high-altitude section. Allow sensible connections, recovery after travelling through the Andes and time for a separate flight from mainland Ecuador to the Galapagos.

### When should visa and payment rules be checked?

Before the final purchase of international flights, then again before departure, taking account of citizenship, route and dates. Travelling with an organiser does not replace individual immigration requirements.
